items.title: Bobby Johnson Jr. interviewed by Monk Rowe, Ellenville, New York, June 23, 1998
items.q: So one of the A&R men I think was Russ Case, a fine trumpet player, he was RCA Victor’s A&R man. He said let’s go back and try the first one.

ctx.x: The recording session where you did “Tippin’ In” with the mute?

Well how this came about, we had rehearsed “Tippin In” it was written by Bobby Smith. We had rehearsed it in Boston. And at that particular time the union was on strike. [Scats] which had like a wartime flavor. So we were supposed to come to New York but they told us instead of coming to New York, since we was already out west, to go to RCA Victor out by the stockyards in Chicago. So about five below zero I think that morning, we went and we’d all been drinking that night for some reason, I don’t know why, we’d…
